compression_benchmarks.detail: The recorded ByteLang sample was 179644 bytes after excluding build/git/editor metadata. CAT v0.7+gzip was 37131 bytes, 934 bytes larger than tar.gz at 36197 bytes; compact v0.8+gzip saved only 9 bytes versus v0.7+gzip. Zstd 1.5.7 level 3 did not beat CAT+gzip for size on that tree; level 19 wrapped around plain CAT reduced size to 28561 bytes, with a slower single-run encode including process startup. Tar.zst level 19 was 27349 bytes. Random/already-compressed inputs showed little or no gain. Single-run timings are indicative and use different timer boundaries. The same synthetic corpus was also run on the Pi Zero 2 W with the current v0.7/v0.8 binary; it shows the same size ranking across v0.7, v0.8, gzip, tar.gz, and ZIP, while timing is much slower on the Pi.
